sanskrit: tam uttīrṇaṃ mahābāhuṃ gadāhastam ariṃdamam menire sarvabhūtāni daṇḍahastam ivāntakam
english: As that mighty-armed subduer of foes rose up from the water, mace in hand, all beings beheld him as Death himself, the rod of doom in his grasp.

sanskrit: vajrahastaṃ yathā śakraṃ śūlahastaṃ yathā haram dadṛśuḥ sarvapāñcālāḥ putraṃ tava janādhipa
english: Like Śakra with the thunderbolt in his hand, like Hara with the trident in his, all the Pāñcālas, O lord of men, gazed upon your son.

sanskrit: tam uttīrṇaṃ tu saṃprekṣya samahṛṣyanta sarvaśaḥ pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍaveyāś ca te 'nyonyasya talān daduḥ
english: But seeing him risen from the water, the Pāñcālas and the sons of Pāṇḍu thrilled with joy on every side and struck their palms against one another.

sanskrit: avahāsaṃ tu taṃ matvā putro duryodhanas tava udvṛtya nayane kruddho didhakṣur iva pāṇḍavān
english: But taking that for mockery, your son Duryodhana, enraged, rolled his eyes wide as though he would burn the Pāṇḍavas to ash.

sanskrit: triśikhāṃ bhrukuṭīṃ kṛtvā saṃdaṣṭadaśanacchadaḥ pratyuvāca tatas tān vai pāṇḍavān sahakeśavān
english: Knitting his brow into a threefold furrow and biting his lip, he then made answer to the Pāṇḍavas and Keśava among them.

sanskrit: avahāsasya vo 'syādya prativaktāsmi pāṇḍavāḥ gamiṣyatha hatāḥ sadyaḥ sapāñcālā yamakṣayam
english: "This mockery of yours I shall answer this very day, O Pāṇḍavas. Slain on the instant, you and the Pāñcālas with you shall go to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: utthitas tu jalāt tasmāt putro duryodhanas tava atiṣṭhata gadāpāṇī rudhireṇa samukṣitaḥ
english: Risen from those waters, your son Duryodhana stood firm, mace in hand, drenched and bespattered with blood.

sanskrit: tasya śoṇitadigdhasya salilena samukṣitam śarīraṃ sma tadā bhāti sravann iva mahīdharaḥ
english: His body, smeared with gore and sprinkled with water, shone then like a mountain streaming with red ochre.

sanskrit: tam udyatagadaṃ vīraṃ menire tatra pāṇḍavāḥ vaivasvatam iva kruddhaṃ kiṃkarodyatapāṇinam
english: Beholding that hero with mace upraised, the Pāṇḍavas there took him for the wrathful son of Vivasvat, his attendants standing with weapons lifted.

sanskrit: sa meghaninado harṣān nadann iva ca govṛṣaḥ ājuhāva tataḥ pārthān gadayā yudhi vīryavān
english: Roaring like a thundercloud, bellowing in his joy like a mighty bull, that valiant one then summoned the Pārthas to battle with his mace.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ekaikena ca māṃ yūyam āsīdata yudhiṣṭhira na hy eko bahubhir nyāyyo vīra yodhayituṃ yudhi
english: Duryodhana said: Come against me one by one, O Yudhiṣṭhira; for it is not right, O hero, that one should be made to fight against many in battle.

sanskrit: nyastavarmā viśeṣeṇa śrāntaś cāpsu pariplutaḥ bhṛśaṃ vikṣatagātraś ca hatavāhanasainikaḥ
english: And the more so when one has laid aside his armour, is weary and drenched in the waters, his limbs sorely gashed, his mounts and soldiers slain.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca nābhūd iyaṃ tava prajñā katham evaṃ suyodhana yadābhimanyuṃ bahavo jaghnur yudhi mahārathāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Where was this wisdom of yours, Suyodhana, when many great chariot-warriors together slew Abhimanyu in the fight?

sanskrit: āmuñca kavacaṃ vīra mūrdhajān yamayasva ca yac cānyad api te nāsti tad apy ādatsva bhārata imam ekaṃ ca te kāmaṃ vīra bhūyo dadāmy aham
english: Put on your armour, O hero, and bind up your hair; and whatever else you lack, take that too, O Bhārata. This one wish besides, O hero, I now grant you.

sanskrit: pañcānāṃ pāṇḍaveyānāṃ yena yoddhum ihecchasi taṃ hatvā vai bhavān rājā hato vā svargam āpnuhi ṛte ca jīvitād vīra yuddhe kiṃ kurma te priyam
english: Of the five sons of Pāṇḍu, choose whomever you wish to fight here; having slain him you shall be king, or being slain attain heaven. What, O hero, save your life itself, can we do to please you in this combat?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tatas tava suto rājan varma jagrāha kāñcanam vicitraṃ ca śirastrāṇaṃ jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then your son, O king, took up his golden armour and a wondrous helmet adorned with the gold of the Jambū river.

sanskrit: so 'vabaddhaśirastrāṇaḥ śubhakāñcanavarmabhṛt rarāja rājan putras te kāñcanaḥ śailarāḍ iva
english: With his helmet fastened on and wearing his fair golden mail, your son shone, O king, like a golden mountain-king.

sanskrit: saṃnaddhaḥ sa gadī rājan sajjaḥ saṃgrāmamūrdhani abravīt pāṇḍavān sarvān putro duryodhanas tava
english: Armed and mace in hand, made ready at the forefront of battle, your son Duryodhana spoke, O king, to all the Pāṇḍavas:

sanskrit: bhrātṝṇāṃ bhavatām eko yudhyatāṃ gadayā mayā sahadevena vā yotsye bhīmena nakulena vā
english: "Let one of you brothers fight with me, mace to mace. I will fight with Sahadeva, or with Bhīma, or with Nakula,

sanskrit: atha vā phalgunenādya tvayā vā bharatarṣabha yotsye 'haṃ saṃgaraṃ prāpya vijeṣye ca raṇājire
english: or with Phalguna this day, or with you yourself, O bull of the Bharatas. Joining battle, I shall conquer on the field of war.

sanskrit: aham adya gamiṣyāmi vairasyāntaṃ sudurgamam gadayā puruṣavyāghra hemapaṭṭavinaddhayā
english: This day, O tiger among men, I shall reach the far and hardly-won end of this enmity, with my mace bound about with bands of gold.

sanskrit: gadāyuddhe na me kaś cit sadṛśo 'stīti cintaya gadayā vo haniṣyāmi sarvān eva samāgatān gṛhṇātu sa gadāṃ yo vai yudhyate 'dya mayā saha
english: Be sure of this: in mace-combat there is none my equal. With my mace I shall slay you all, even should you come together. Let him who will fight with me this day take up his mace."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evaṃ duryodhane rājan garjamāne muhur muhuḥ yudhiṣṭhirasya saṃkruddho vāsudevo 'bravīd idam
english: Saṃjaya said: As Duryodhana roared thus again and again, O king, Vāsudeva, wroth with Yudhiṣṭhira, spoke these words:

sanskrit: yadi nāma hy ayaṃ yuddhe varayet tvāṃ yudhiṣṭhira arjunaṃ nakulaṃ vāpi sahadevam athāpi vā
english: "If indeed, O Yudhiṣṭhira, he should choose for combat you, or Arjuna, or Nakula, or even Sahadeva—

sanskrit: kim idaṃ sāhasaṃ rājaṃs tvayā vyāhṛtam īdṛśam ekam eva nihatyājau bhava rājā kuruṣv iti
english: what is this rashness, O king, that you have uttered, saying, 'Slay but one of us in the fight and be king among the Kurus'?

sanskrit: etena hi kṛtā yogyā varṣāṇīha trayodaśa āyase puruṣe rājan bhīmasenajighāṃsayā
english: For thirteen years has he practised here, O king, upon a man of iron, in his longing to slay Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nāma bhavet kāryam asmābhir bharatarṣabha sāhasaṃ kṛtavāṃs tvaṃ tu hy anukrośān nṛpottama
english: How then shall our purpose be accomplished, O bull of the Bharatas? Out of compassion, O best of kings, you have done a rash thing.

sanskrit: nānyam asyānupaśyāmi pratiyoddhāram āhave ṛte vṛkodarāt pārthāt sa ca nātikṛtaśramaḥ
english: I see no other fit to meet him in battle save Vṛkodara, son of Pṛthā—and even he is not greatly practised.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ dyūtam ārabdhaṃ punar eva yathā purā viṣamaṃ śakuneś caiva tava caiva viśāṃ pate
english: So this gambling-match is begun again as of old, the same crooked game of Śakuni's and of yours, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: balī bhīmaḥ samarthaś ca kṛtī rājā suyodhanaḥ balavān vā kṛtī veti kṛtī rājan viśiṣyate
english: Bhīma is strong and able, but King Suyodhana is skilled. Between strength and skill, O king, the skilled man prevails.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ rājaṃs tvayā śatruḥ same pathi niveśitaḥ nyastaś cātmā suviṣame kṛcchram āpāditā vayam
english: Thus, O king, you have set the enemy upon even ground and staked yourself upon a perilous one; you have brought us into sore distress.

sanskrit: ko nu sarvān vinirjitya śatrūn ekena vairiṇā paṇitvā caikapāṇena rocayed evam āhavam
english: What man, having vanquished all his foes, would choose to gamble it all on a single throw with one remaining adversary, and so take pleasure in such a fight?

sanskrit: na hi paśyāmi taṃ loke gadāhastaṃ narottamam yudhyed duryodhanaṃ saṃkhye kṛtitvād dhi viśeṣayet
english: For I see not in the world that best of men, mace in hand, who could fight Duryodhana in battle and by his skill surpass him—

sanskrit: phalgunaṃ vā bhavantaṃ vā mādrīputrāv athāpi vā na samarthān ahaṃ manye gadāhastasya saṃyuge
english: neither Phalguna, nor yourself, nor the two sons of Mādrī do I deem a match for that mace-wielder in the fray.

sanskrit: sa kathaṃ vadase śatruṃ yudhyasva gadayeti ha ekaṃ ca no nihatyājau bhava rājeti bhārata
english: How then, O Bhārata, do you tell the foe, 'Fight with the mace, and having slain but one of us in battle be king'?

sanskrit: vṛkodaraṃ samāsādya saṃśayo vijaye hi naḥ nyāyato yudhyamānānāṃ kṛtī hy eṣa mahābalaḥ
english: Even when Vṛkodara meets him, our victory is in doubt should they fight by the rules; for this man is skilled and of great might."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca madhusūdana mā kārṣīr viṣādaṃ yadunandana adya pāraṃ gamiṣyāmi vairasya bhṛśadurgamam
english: Bhīma said: O slayer of Madhu, give way to no despair, O joy of the Yadus. This day I shall reach the farther shore of this enmity, so hard to cross.

sanskrit: ahaṃ suyodhanaṃ saṃkhye haniṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ vijayo vai dhruvaṃ kṛṣṇa dharmarājasya dṛśyate
english: I shall slay Suyodhana in battle, of that there is no doubt. Victory for the King of Righteousness, O Kṛṣṇa, is seen for certain.

sanskrit: adhyardhena guṇeneyaṃ gadā gurutarī mama na tathā dhārtarāṣṭrasya mā kārṣīr mādhava vyathām
english: This mace of mine is heavier by half again than that of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son. Be not troubled, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: sāmarān api lokāṃs trīn nānāśastradharān yudhi yodhayeyaṃ raṇe hṛṣṭaḥ kim utādya suyodhanam
english: The three worlds with the gods themselves, bearing weapons of every kind, would I gladly fight in battle—how much more, this day, Suyodhana!

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathā saṃbhāṣamāṇaṃ tu vāsudevo vṛkodaram hṛṣṭaḥ saṃpūjayām āsa vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: As Vṛkodara spoke thus, Vāsudeva, rejoicing, honoured him and spoke these words:

sanskrit: tvām āśritya mahābāho dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nihatāriḥ svakāṃ dīptāṃ śriyaṃ prāpto na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Leaning upon you, O mighty-armed one, the King of Righteousness Yudhiṣṭhira, his foes slain, shall surely regain his own resplendent fortune, of that there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tvayā vinihatāḥ sarve dhṛtarāṣṭrasutā raṇe rājāno rājaputrāś ca nāgāś ca vinipātitāḥ
english: By you have all the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra been laid low in battle, and kings and princes and elephants struck down.

sanskrit: kaliṅgā māgadhāḥ prācyā gāndhārāḥ kuravas tathā tvām āsādya mahāyuddhe nihatāḥ pāṇḍunandana
english: The Kaliṅgas, the Māgadhas, the Easterners, the Gāndhāras, and the Kurus, meeting you in the great battle, were slain, O joy of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: hatvā duryodhanaṃ cāpi prayacchorvīṃ sasāgarām dharmarājāya kaunteya yathā viṣṇuḥ śacīpateḥ
english: Having slain Duryodhana too, O son of Kuntī, give over the sea-girt earth to the King of Righteousness, as Viṣṇu gave it to the lord of Śacī.

sanskrit: tvāṃ ca prāpya raṇe pāpo dhārtarāṣṭro vinaṅkṣyati tvam asya sakthinī bhaṅktvā pratijñāṃ pārayiṣyasi
english: Meeting you in battle, the wicked son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra shall perish; breaking both his thighs, you shall fulfil your vow.

sanskrit: yatnena tu sadā pārtha yoddhavyo dhṛtarāṣṭrajaḥ kṛtī ca balavāṃś caiva yuddhaśauṇḍaś ca nityadā
english: Yet the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra must ever be fought with care, O Pārtha; he is skilled and strong, and at all times a connoisseur of battle."

sanskrit: tatas tu sātyakī rājan pūjayām āsa pāṇḍavam vividhābhiś ca tāṃ vāgbhiḥ pūjayām āsa mādhavaḥ
english: Then Sātyaki, O king, honoured the son of Pāṇḍu, and with words of many kinds Mādhava too honoured him.

sanskrit: pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍaveyāś ca dharmarājapurogamāḥ tad vaco bhīmasenasya sarva evābhyapūjayan
english: The Pāñcālas and the sons of Pāṇḍu, with the King of Righteousness at their head, all alike applauded those words of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tato bhīmabalo bhīmo yudhiṣṭhiram athābravīt sṛñjayaiḥ saha tiṣṭhantaṃ tapantam iva bhāskaram
english: Then Bhīma of terrible strength spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira, who stood amid the Sṛñjayas, blazing like the sun:

sanskrit: aham etena saṃgamya saṃyuge yoddhum utsahe na hi śakto raṇe jetuṃ mām eṣa puruṣādhamaḥ
english: "Joining with him, I am eager to fight in this combat. This basest of men is not able to vanquish me in battle.

sanskrit: adya krodhaṃ vimokṣyāmi nihitaṃ hṛdaye bhṛśam suyodhane dhārtarāṣṭre khāṇḍave 'gnim ivārjunaḥ
english: This day I shall loose upon Suyodhana, son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the wrath long pent and brooding in my heart, as Arjuna loosed the fire upon the Khāṇḍava forest.

sanskrit: śalyam adyoddhariṣyāmi tava pāṇḍava hṛcchayam nihatya gadayā pāpam adya rājan sukhī bhava
english: This day I shall draw forth the dart that lies in your heart, O son of Pāṇḍu. Having slain the wicked one with my mace, be happy this day, O king.

sanskrit: adya kīrtimayīṃ mālāṃ pratimokṣye tavānagha prāṇāñ śriyaṃ ca rājyaṃ ca mokṣyate 'dya suyodhanaḥ
english: This day I shall set upon you a garland woven of glory, O sinless one; this day Suyodhana shall let go of his life, his fortune, and his kingdom.

sanskrit: rājā ca dhṛtarāṣṭro 'dya śrutvā putraṃ mayā hatam smariṣyaty aśubhaṃ karma yat tac chakunibuddhijam
english: And King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, hearing this day that his son is slain by me, shall remember that evil deed which was born of Śakuni's counsel."

sanskrit: ity uktvā bharataśreṣṭho gadām udyamya vīryavān udatiṣṭhata yuddhāya śakro vṛtram ivāhvayan
english: Having spoken thus, that best and most valiant of the Bharatas raised his mace and rose up for the fight, as Śakra rose to challenge Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tam ekākinam āsādya dhārtarāṣṭraṃ mahābalam niryūtham iva mātaṅgaṃ samahṛṣyanta pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Coming upon the mighty son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who stood alone like an elephant strayed from its herd, the Pāṇḍavas thrilled with joy.

sanskrit: tam udyatagadaṃ dṛṣṭvā kailāsam iva śṛṅgiṇam bhīmasenas tadā rājan duryodhanam athābravīt
english: Seeing him with mace upraised, peaked like Kailāsa, Bhīmasena then, O king, spoke to Duryodhana:

sanskrit: rājñāpi dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa tvayā cāsmāsu yat kṛtam smara tad duṣkṛtaṃ karma yad vṛttaṃ vāraṇāvate
english: "Recall that evil deed which King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and you wrought against us—what came to pass at Vāraṇāvata.

sanskrit: draupadī ca parikliṣṭā sabhāmadhye rajasvalā dyūte yad vijito rājā śakuner buddhiniścayāt
english: Recall how Draupadī, in her courses, was tormented in the midst of the assembly, when the king was won at dice by the settled cunning of Śakuni.

sanskrit: yāni cānyāni duṣṭātman pāpāni kṛtavān asi anāgaḥsu ca pārtheṣu tasya paśya mahat phalam
english: And whatever other sins, O evil-souled one, you have wrought against the blameless sons of Pṛthā—behold now the great fruit thereof.

sanskrit: tvatkṛte nihataḥ śete śaratalpe mahāyaśāḥ gāṅgeyo bharataśreṣṭhaḥ sarveṣāṃ naḥ pitāmahaḥ
english: For your sake the son of Gaṅgā, the glorious best of the Bharatas, the grandsire of us all, lies slain upon a bed of arrows.

sanskrit: hato droṇaś ca karṇaś ca hataḥ śalyaḥ pratāpavān vairasya cādikartāsau śakunir nihato yudhi
english: Slain is Droṇa, and Karṇa, and slain is the mighty Śalya; and Śakuni, the first author of this enmity, has been slain in battle.

sanskrit: bhrātaras te hatāḥ śūrāḥ putrāś ca sahasainikāḥ rājānaś ca hatāḥ śūrāḥ samareṣv anivartinaḥ
english: Slain are your valiant brothers, and your sons together with their soldiers; slain too are the brave kings who never turned back in battle.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca nihatā bahavaḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ prātikāmī tathā pāpo draupadyāḥ kleśakṛd dhataḥ
english: These and many other bulls among the kṣatriyas have been slain; and the wicked Prātikāmin too, who wrought Draupadī's affliction, has been slain.

sanskrit: avaśiṣṭas tvam evaikaḥ kulaghno 'dhamapūruṣaḥ tvām apy adya haniṣyāmi gadayā nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: You alone are left, destroyer of your line, basest of men; and you too this day shall I slay with my mace—herein is no doubt.

sanskrit: adya te 'haṃ raṇe darpaṃ sarvaṃ nāśayitā nṛpa rājyāśāṃ vipulāṃ rājan pāṇḍaveṣu ca duṣkṛtam
english: This day, O king, in battle I shall destroy all your pride, and your vast hope of kingdom, and the wrong you did the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca kiṃ katthitena bahudhā yudhyasvādya mayā saha adya te 'haṃ vineṣyāmi yuddhaśraddhāṃ vṛkodara
english: Duryodhana said: What use this boasting in so many ways? Fight with me now. This day, O Vṛkodara, I shall take from you all appetite for battle.

sanskrit: kiṃ na paśyasi māṃ pāpa gadāyuddhe vyavasthitam himavacchikharākārāṃ pragṛhya mahatīṃ gadām
english: Do you not see me, O sinner, standing ready for the mace-fight, gripping a mighty mace shaped like a Himālayan peak?

sanskrit: gadinaṃ ko 'dya māṃ pāpa jetum utsahate ripuḥ nyāyato yudhyamānasya deveṣv api puraṃdaraḥ
english: What foe, O sinner, dares this day hope to vanquish me, mace in hand and fighting by the rules—not even Purandara among the gods?

sanskrit: mā vṛthā garja kaunteya śāradābhram ivājalam darśayasva balaṃ yuddhe yāvat tat te 'dya vidyate
english: Roar not in vain, O son of Kuntī, like a rainless autumn cloud. Show in battle what strength is yours this day.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā pāñcālāḥ sahasṛñjayāḥ sarve saṃpūjayām āsus tad vaco vijigīṣavaḥ
english: Hearing those words of his, the Pāñcālas together with the Sṛñjayas, all longing for victory, applauded that speech.

sanskrit: taṃ mattam iva mātaṅgaṃ talaśabdena mānavāḥ bhūyaḥ saṃharṣayām āsū rājan duryodhanaṃ nṛpam
english: As one rouses a maddened elephant, the men, O king, with the clapping of their hands urged King Duryodhana on yet more.

sanskrit: bṛṃhanti kuñjarās tatra hayā heṣanti cāsakṛt śastrāṇi saṃpradīpyante pāṇḍavānāṃ jayaiṣiṇām
english: There the elephants trumpeted, the horses neighed again and again, and the weapons of the victory-seeking Pāṇḍavas blazed forth.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmin yuddhe mahārāja saṃpravṛtte sudāruṇe upaviṣṭeṣu sarveṣu pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu
english: Saṃjaya said: When that most terrible combat had begun, O great king, and all the high-souled Pāṇḍavas had taken their seats,

sanskrit: tatas tāladhvajo rāmas tayor yuddha upasthite śrutvā tac chiṣyayo rājann ājagāma halāyudhaḥ
english: then Rāma of the palm-tree banner, the bearer of the plough, hearing that combat between his two pupils was at hand, came near, O king.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaprītāḥ pūjayitvā narādhipāḥ śiṣyayoḥ kauśalaṃ yuddhe paśya rāmeti cābruvan
english: Seeing him, the kings, well pleased, did him honour and said, "Behold, O Rāma, the skill of your two pupils in battle."

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā rāmo dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ ca pāṇḍavam duryodhanaṃ ca kauravyaṃ gadāpāṇim avasthitam
english: And then Rāma, beholding Kṛṣṇa and the son of Pāṇḍu, and Duryodhana of the Kuru line standing with mace in hand, spoke:

sanskrit: catvāriṃśad ahāny adya dve ca me niḥsṛtasya vai puṣyeṇa saṃprayāto 'smi śravaṇe punarāgataḥ śiṣyayor vai gadāyuddhaṃ draṣṭukāmo 'smi mādhava
english: "Forty days and two are gone this day since I set forth; I departed under the asterism Puṣya and am returned under Śravaṇa. I long, O Mādhava, to see the mace-combat of my two pupils."

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā pariṣvajya halāyudham svāgataṃ kuśalaṃ cāsmai paryapṛcchad yathātatham
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, embracing the bearer of the plough, bade him welcome and duly enquired after his well-being.
